text:
amar: Ran a long-seqlen repro for the KV cache thrash on prod-staging. Seqlen=8192, batch=2, microbatching off. HBM climbs and then we get eviction waves every ~120ms. nsys attached. Anybody free to eyeball?
sam: grabbing the nsys now. quick question — did you force flash_attn kernel or let kernel selector pick?
amar: let selector pick (auto-kernel), but I tried a manual run forcing cuDNN attn and the thrash reduced a bit at the cost of higher peak SM utilization.
perf-bot: nsys summary uploaded: peak_hbm_bandwidth=356.2 GB/s, sustained_window(0.5s)=298 GB/s, top_kernels=[attention_kv_read, flash_attn_backward, kv_page_scan], cpu-migrations seen when eviction starts. perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234
lucy: do you have the KV cache hit ratio over time? eviction waves sound like repeated full-table scans.
amar: hit ratio drops from 98% -> 47% when seq>4096 and requests include streaming prefix resets. I suspected KV fragmentation + big prefix churn.
sam: opening the trace, I see attention_kv_read has long memcpy spikes followed by lots of small kernels. Could be inefficient page granularity in our slab allocator.
jess: could also be a batching heuristic problem — with long seqs our continuous-batcher keeps combining requests, growing working set beyond HBM capacity. Have we tried enforcing microbatch cap or early flush?
amar: tried cap=1024 tokens per batch and that cut peak HBM by ~30% but added tail latency. Still get repeated KV eviction activity in the nsys timeline.
sam: screenshot from timeline: "kernel timeline: flash_attn_backward (cudaStream0) -> attention_kv_read (cudaStream1) -> kv_page_scan (cudaStream1) repeated". Looks like cross-stream synchronizations causing gaps.
lucy: two action items: (1) reproduce with allocator metricting on (slab/large-page stats), (2) try pinning kernel selection to cuDNN-attn + small batch microcap to see if eviction stops.
amar: doing (1) now, enabling SLAB_DEBUG, allocator dump after 30s.
perf-bot: nvprof-style top kernels: flash_attn_backward: 42.1% time, attention_kv_read: 24.7%, kv_page_scan: 13.5%. Note: repeated small kernels increase kernel launch overhead and prevent sustained HBM prefetch.
sam: hypothesis — when prefix resets are common we thrash KV because our LRU isn't hot/live-aware; big sequence entries are pinned then scanned. Could try shrink-to-fit on heavy prefixes or prefix-aware TTL.
jess: also consider changing kernel selection policy: prefer kernels that keep KV access coalesced even if compute is slightly worse. We should surface a policy flag and run A/B on repro.
amar: quick repro command I ran: 
```
nsys profile -o kv-thrash --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=cpu ./run_infer --model x --batch 2 --seqlen 8192 --kv-mode slab
```
attached the raw .qdrep in the trace blob.
lucy: if allocator shows many small allocations and deallocs around 1-4MB, that aligns with slab fragmentation. Plan: (A) run with large-page slab arena, (B) force cuDNN attn, (C) cap continuous-batcher to 1024 tokens. We'll compare HBM_peak and eviction_count.
sam: I'll iterate on a runtime patch to coalesce KV reads into fewer launches (group pages into bigger memcpy). If we can reduce small memcpy floods, HBM will be more stable.
amar: thanks — I'll run the three configs and post numbers. If anyone has other quick knobs (quantized KV compactors?) drop here. :thumbsup:
jess: adding a note — if coalescing causes higher latency on the critical path we may need a dynamic policy: coalesce only when backend HBM_free<threshold.
perf-bot: scheduled follow-up: run-diff matrix queued (A/B/C) — results expected in ~4h.
